editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a high-tech building where a science meeting turns into a bloodbath in seconds. You follow Professor Se-jeong, who goes from giving a speech to fighting for her life when a weird virus leaks out. The government locks all the doors from the outside, leaving you and a few other survivors trapped with people who are turning into monsters right before your eyes. It feels like a nightmare where the walls are closing in, and you never know who is going to get bitten next. The vibe is tense and scary, making you feel every bit of the panic the characters are going through.

What really works here is how fast the action moves and how gross the monster designs are. The acting is solid, and the twists keep you guessing until the very end. While some of the dialogue feels a bit stiff, the fight scenes more than make up for it. If you love creature features, you should definitely check this out. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the gory details, or just rent it on Apple TV for a movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the final act, you find out that Se-jeong is actually immune to the virus because of a secret treatment she took years ago. She manages to lure the remaining monsters into a lab chamber and blows it up, clearing a path to the exit. However, the twist is that the government planned the leak to test the virus on humans. Se-jeong escapes the building, but she realizes the virus has already leaked into the city outside.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves zombie movies and high-stakes survival stories.
